# core/sort.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/sort.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

Sorting and searching vectors of `u64`, and sorting
indices by a key.

To sort records by a field, put the field in a key vector and sort the
indices `0..n` with `sort_by_key_u64`: that is a stable sort. Insertion
sort (`sort_u64`) is quadratic in the worst case; on 50,000 random words
it takes 4.8 s where `merge_sort_u64` takes 0.02 s.

What is proved: a sort leaves the vector sorted (spec fn `sorted`, or
`sorted_by_key`) and a permutation of what it was (`same_elems`: the same
length and each value as many times, stated with `vcount`); a search of a
vector known to be sorted is exact, and searching one not known to be
sorted is rejected at compile time. The merge sort deals the vector into
two, sorts each, and merges them by popping the larger tail, so every step
of its proof is about the ends of vectors and the counts in them.

`import "core/sort.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md).

| [`merge_sort_u64`](#merge_sort_u64) | Sorts `v` in ascending order in O(n log n) time (merge sort, with insertion sort below 16 elements). |
| [`sort_by_key_u64`](#sort_by_key_u64) | Sorts `v`, a vector of indices into `keys`, by key. |
| [`lower_bound_u64`](#lower_bound_u64) | The first index whose element is at least `x` (`vlen(v)` if none is). |
| [`sorted_contains_u64`](#sorted_contains_u64) | `x` is an element of the sorted vector `v`. |
| [`sorted_find_u64`](#sorted_find_u64) | The index of `x` in the sorted vector `v`, if it occurs. |
| [`vec_find_u64`](#vec_find_u64) | The index of the first `x` in `v`, if it occurs (a linear scan; `v` need not be sorted). |
| [`vec_min_u64`](#vec_min_u64) | The smallest element of `v`, which must not be empty. |
| [`vec_max_u64`](#vec_max_u64) | The largest element of `v`, which must not be empty. |
| [`vec_reverse_u64`](#vec_reverse_u64) | Reverses `v` in place. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `sort_u64`

```bastio
fn sort_u64(v: &mut Vec[u64])
  ensures same_elems(v, old(v)) && sorted(v)
```

Sorts `v` in ascending order (insertion sort: fast for short or nearly
sorted vectors, quadratic in the worst case). The result is proved
sorted and a permutation of the input.

Example:

```bastio
let mut v = vec_new[u64]();
vec_push(&mut v, 30);
vec_push(&mut v, 10);
vec_push(&mut v, 20);
sort_u64(&mut v);
assert sorted(v) && vlen(v) == 3;
// Sorted, so the binary searches below need no further proof.
let at = lower_bound_u64(v, 20);
let has = sorted_contains_u64(v, 20) && !sorted_contains_u64(v, 25);
let ok = vec_get(v, 0) == 10 && vec_get(v, 2) == 30 && at == 1 && has;
vec_free(v);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `merge_sort_u64`

```bastio
fn merge_sort_u64(v: &mut Vec[u64])
  ensures same_elems(v, old(v)) && sorted(v)
```

Sorts `v` in ascending order in O(n log n) time (merge sort, with
insertion sort below 16 elements). Proved sorted and a permutation of
the input, as `sort_u64` is. Uses `n` words of extra memory.

Example:

```bastio
let mut v = vec_new[u64]();
let mut x: u64 = 7;
let mut i = 0;
while i < 1000
  invariant i <= 1000 && vlen(v) == i && x < 2147483648
{
  x = (x * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648;
  vec_push(&mut v, x % 1000);
  i = i + 1;
}
merge_sort_u64(&mut v);
assert sorted(v) && vlen(v) == 1000;
let ok = vec_get(v, 0) <= vec_get(v, 999);
vec_free(v);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `sort_by_key_u64`

```bastio
fn sort_by_key_u64(v: &mut Vec[u64], keys: &Vec[u64])
  requires all_indices_below(v, vlen(keys))
  ensures same_elems(v, old(v)) && sorted_by_key(v, keys)
```

Sorts `v`, a vector of indices into `keys`, by key: afterwards
`keys[v[0]] <= keys[v[1]] <= ...`, indices with equal keys ascend, and
`v` holds the same indices. Sorting `0..n` this way is a stable sort of
n records by a field. Merge sort, O(n log n).

Example:

```bastio
// Records 0..4 with an age each; sort the record numbers by age.
let mut ages = vec_new[u64]();
vec_push(&mut ages, 30);
vec_push(&mut ages, 20);
vec_push(&mut ages, 30);
vec_push(&mut ages, 10);
let mut idx = vec_new[u64]();
vec_push(&mut idx, 0);
vec_push(&mut idx, 1);
vec_push(&mut idx, 2);
vec_push(&mut idx, 3);
sort_by_key_u64(&mut idx, ages);
// Every element is still an index into `ages`, so reading it needs no check.
let youngest = vec_get(ages, vec_get(idx, 0));
// 3 (10), 1 (20), then 0 and 2 (both 30) in their original order.
let ok = youngest == 10 && vec_get(idx, 1) == 1 && vec_get(idx, 2) == 0 && vec_get(idx, 3) == 2;
vec_free(idx);
vec_free(ages);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `lower_bound_u64`

```bastio
fn lower_bound_u64(v: &Vec[u64], x: u64) -> u64
  requires sorted(v)
  ensures result <= vlen(v)
  ensures forall k: u64 :: k < result ==> vget(v, k) < x
  ensures forall k: u64 :: result <= k && k < vlen(v) ==> vget(v, k) >= x
```

The first index whose element is at least `x` (`vlen(v)` if none is):
where `x` is, or would be inserted, in a sorted vector.

Example:

```bastio
let mut v = vec_new[u64]();
vec_push(&mut v, 2);
vec_push(&mut v, 4);
vec_push(&mut v, 4);
vec_push(&mut v, 8);
assert sorted(v);   // pushed in order, which the prover follows
let a = lower_bound_u64(v, 4);   // the first 4
let b = lower_bound_u64(v, 5);   // where 5 would go
let c = lower_bound_u64(v, 9);   // past the end
vec_free(v);
if a != 1 || b != 3 || c != 4 { return 1; }
```

### `sorted_contains_u64`

```bastio
fn sorted_contains_u64(v: &Vec[u64], x: u64) -> bool
  requires sorted(v)
  ensures result == !(forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(v) ==> vget(v, k) != x)
```

`x` is an element of the sorted vector `v`.

### `sorted_find_u64`

```bastio
fn sorted_find_u64(v: &Vec[u64], x: u64) -> Option[u64]
  requires sorted(v)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some < vlen(v) && vget(v, result.Some) == x
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> (forall k: u64 :: k < result.Some ==> vget(v, k) != x)
  ensures result is Option::None ==> (forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(v) ==> vget(v, k) != x)
```

The index of `x` in the sorted vector `v`, if it occurs: the first
one, when it occurs more than once. A binary search.

Example:

```bastio
let mut v = vec_new[u64]();
vec_push(&mut v, 10);
vec_push(&mut v, 20);
vec_push(&mut v, 20);
vec_push(&mut v, 40);
let a = sorted_find_u64(v, 20);
let b = sorted_find_u64(v, 30);
assert b is Option::None ==> (forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(v) ==> vget(v, k) != 30);
let ok = opt_or[u64](a, 9) == 1 && b is Option::None;
vec_free(v);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `vec_find_u64`

```bastio
fn vec_find_u64(v: &Vec[u64], x: u64) -> Option[u64]
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some < vlen(v) && vget(v, result.Some) == x
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> (forall k: u64 :: k < result.Some ==> vget(v, k) != x)
  ensures result is Option::None ==> (forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(v) ==> vget(v, k) != x)
```

The index of the first `x` in `v`, if it occurs (a linear scan; `v`
need not be sorted).

Example:

```bastio
let mut v = vec_new[u64]();
vec_push(&mut v, 7);
vec_push(&mut v, 3);
vec_push(&mut v, 7);
let mut at = 9;
match vec_find_u64(v, 7) {
  Option::Some(i) => {
    assert vget(v, i) == 7;   // proved, so the index needs no check
    at = i;
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
let none = vec_find_u64(v, 5);
vec_free(v);
if at != 0 || none is Option::Some { return 1; }
```

### `vec_min_u64`

```bastio
fn vec_min_u64(v: &Vec[u64]) -> u64
  requires 0 < vlen(v)
  ensures forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(v) ==> result <= vget(v, k)
  ensures !(forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(v) ==> vget(v, k) != result)
```

The smallest element of `v`, which must not be empty.

Example:

```bastio
let mut v = vec_new[u64]();
vec_push(&mut v, 5);
vec_push(&mut v, 2);
vec_push(&mut v, 9);
let lo = vec_min_u64(v);
let hi = vec_max_u64(v);
assert lo <= vget(v, 0) && hi >= vget(v, 2);   // proved bounds
vec_free(v);
if lo != 2 || hi != 9 { return 1; }
```

### `vec_max_u64`

```bastio
fn vec_max_u64(v: &Vec[u64]) -> u64
  requires 0 < vlen(v)
  ensures forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(v) ==> vget(v, k) <= result
  ensures !(forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(v) ==> vget(v, k) != result)
```

The largest element of `v`, which must not be empty.

### `vec_reverse_u64`

```bastio
fn vec_reverse_u64(v: &mut Vec[u64])
  ensures vlen(v) == vlen(old(v))
  ensures forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(v) ==> vget(v, k) == vget(old(v), vlen(v) - 1 - k)
```

Reverses `v` in place.

Example:

```bastio
let mut v = vec_new[u64]();
vec_push(&mut v, 1);
vec_push(&mut v, 2);
vec_push(&mut v, 3);
vec_reverse_u64(&mut v);
assert vlen(v) == 3 && vget(v, 0) == 3 && vget(v, 2) == 1;
vec_free(v);
```

### `vec_contains_u64`

```bastio
fn vec_contains_u64(v: &Vec[u64], x: u64) -> bool
  ensures result == !(forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(v) ==> vget(v, k) != x)
```

`x` is an element of `v` (a linear scan; `v` need not be sorted).

Example:

```bastio
let mut v = vec_new[u64]();
vec_push(&mut v, 5);
vec_push(&mut v, 3);
let ok = vec_contains_u64(v, 3) && !vec_contains_u64(v, 4);
vec_free(v);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `vec_extend_u64`

```bastio
fn vec_extend_u64(dst: &mut Vec[u64], src: &Vec[u64])
  ensures vlen(dst) == vlen(old(dst)) + vlen(src)
  ensures forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(old(dst)) ==> vget(dst, k) == vget(old(dst), k)
  ensures forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(src) ==> vget(dst, vlen(old(dst)) + k) == vget(src, k)
```

Appends every element of `src` to `dst`.

Example:

```bastio
let mut a = vec_new[u64]();
vec_push(&mut a, 1);
let mut b = vec_clone_u64(a);
vec_push(&mut b, 2);
vec_extend_u64(&mut a, b);
assert vlen(a) == 3 && vget(a, 0) == 1 && vget(a, 2) == 2;
vec_free(a);
vec_free(b);
```

### `vec_clone_u64`

```bastio
fn vec_clone_u64(v: &Vec[u64]) -> Vec[u64]
  ensures vlen(result) == vlen(v)
  ensures forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(v) ==> vget(result, k) == vget(v, k)
```

A copy of `v`.

## Specification functions

### `sorted_upto`

```bastio
spec fn sorted_upto(v: &Vec[u64], n: u64) -> bool {
  forall a: u64 :: forall b: u64 :: a < b && b < n ==> vget(v, a) <= vget(v, b)
}
```

Elements `0..n` of `v` are in ascending order.

### `sorted`

```bastio
spec fn sorted(v: &Vec[u64]) -> bool {
  sorted_upto(v, vlen(v))
}
```

`v` is in ascending order.

### `same_elems`

```bastio
spec fn same_elems(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64]) -> bool {
  vlen(a) == vlen(b) && forall x: u64 :: vcount(a, x) == vcount(b, x)
}
```

`a` and `b` hold the same elements, each as many times: one is a
permutation of the other.

### `sorted_desc`

```bastio
spec fn sorted_desc(v: &Vec[u64]) -> bool {
  forall a: u64 :: forall b: u64 :: a < b && b < vlen(v) ==> vget(v, a) >= vget(v, b)
}
```

`v` is in descending order.

### `all_at_most`

```bastio
spec fn all_at_most(v: &Vec[u64], x: u64) -> bool {
  forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(v) ==> vget(v, k) <= x
}
```

Every element of `v` is at most `x`.

### `all_indices_below`

```bastio
spec fn all_indices_below(v: &Vec[u64], n: u64) -> bool {
  forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(v) ==> vget(v, k) < n
}
```

Every element of `v` is less than `n` (an index into a vector of length `n`).

### `key_le`

```bastio
spec fn key_le(keys: &Vec[u64], x: u64, y: u64) -> bool {
  vget(keys, x) < vget(keys, y) || (vget(keys, x) == vget(keys, y) && x <= y)
}
```

Index `x` comes no later than index `y` when sorting by `keys`: a
smaller key first, and on equal keys the smaller index.

### `sorted_by_key`

```bastio
spec fn sorted_by_key(v: &Vec[u64], keys: &Vec[u64]) -> bool {
  all_indices_below(v, vlen(keys)) &&
  (forall a: u64 :: forall b: u64 :: a < b && b < vlen(v) ==> key_le(keys, vget(v, a), vget(v, b)))
}
```

The elements of `v` are indices into `keys`, in ascending order of key,
and indices with equal keys in ascending order.

### `sorted_by_key_desc`

```bastio
spec fn sorted_by_key_desc(v: &Vec[u64], keys: &Vec[u64]) -> bool {
  all_indices_below(v, vlen(keys)) &&
  (forall a: u64 :: forall b: u64 :: a < b && b < vlen(v) ==> key_le(keys, vget(v, b), vget(v, a)))
}
```

The same, in descending order.

### `all_keys_at_most`

```bastio
spec fn all_keys_at_most(v: &Vec[u64], keys: &Vec[u64], x: u64) -> bool {
  forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(v) ==> key_le(keys, vget(v, k), x)
}
```

Every element of `v` comes no later than index `x`.
